rows.name: GitHub Pages (github.io hosted service; not a blog engine)
rows.reason: github.io publishes repository web assets, optionally built. Hosting still needs a blog engine/authoring workflow; it is not the complete self-hosted blogging alternative. Static-generator deployment reference is narrower.

rows.name: Publii
rows.reason: Strong initial fit for visual authoring and a self-hosted static blog. Editor runs locally; if browser-based server administration is required, confirm that distinction before selection.

rows.name: Publii
rows.reason: Publii provides desktop writing and SEO-oriented static publishing to personal hosting without server CMS/database. Editing is desktop-based, not browser-based; back up local projects and verify theme output.

rows.name: WordPress (self-hosted WordPress.org software)
rows.reason: Self-hosted PHP/database blog offers conventional editing, baseline SEO and extensions. Keep themes/extensions proportionate to simplicity; no specific plugin combination was validated.

rows.name: Ghost
rows.reason: Open-source software has documented VPS self-hosting and automatic metadata, sitemaps, canonical tags and structured data. Server administration is a simplicity tradeoff, not a documented violation.

rows.name: Ghost
rows.reason: Ghost offers built-in technical SEO as a server CMS. Server/database administration remains required; verify hosting-guide recommendations against the actual deployed release.

rows.name: Bludit
rows.reason: Bludit offers browser Markdown/visual editing, flat-file JSON and SEO tools. PHP hosting needs maintenance; general SEO claims do not establish every theme's tags or sitemap behavior.

rows.name: HTMLy
rows.reason: HTMLy offers database-free PHP blogging, web/filesystem management and sitemaps. Verify hosting compatibility and theme metadata/canonicals; the opened homepage did not establish them.

rows.name: Hugo
rows.reason: Hugo supports static builds and sitemaps, but theme title, description and canonical output were not inspected. Verify generated HTML before treating the configuration as fully SEO-ready.

rows.name: WordPress
rows.reason: WordPress provides self-hosted visual blogging, themes, search-engine support and optional SEO extensions. It requires a database and ongoing application/theme/plugin maintenance; limit extensions when simplicity matters.

rows.name: Ghost
rows.reason: An open-source publishing engine with documented self-hosted installation and built-in technical SEO; it meets the blogging requirement, with ongoing server maintenance.

rows.name: Ghostscript
rows.reason: A PostScript/PDF interpreter does not provide blog authoring, site publishing, or blog SEO features, so it does not address the requested self-hosted blogging system.

rows.name: Ghost
rows.reason: Self-hostable publishing supplies automatic metadata, canonical tags, XML sitemaps and structured data. Operation/upgrades require ongoing work; wider publishing features may exceed minimal personal-blog needs.

rows.name: Hugo
rows.reason: Hugo generates self-hostable static blogs and XML sitemaps. Themes/configuration determine remaining SEO output; it is not a complete visual CMS and favors simple deployment over browser editing.

rows.name: GitHub Pages (github.io hosted service; not a blog engine)
rows.reason: The specified github.io service hosts static files on GitHub; it is neither a self-hosted deployment nor a standalone blog engine, though generators can publish there.

rows.name: Ghostscript
rows.reason: PostScript/PDF interpreter and graphics library processes documents rather than authoring/publishing blogs. Name similarity establishes no usable blogging-system relationship.
